briefdescription.para: Reusable persistence engine for the API's CRUDS (Create/Read/Update/Delete/Search) operations.

detaileddescription.para: Sits below the request-facing controllers (EntityController and its derived classes). It owns the single DatabaseController obtained from the Store singleton, turns an entity's SQL-builder methods into parameterized statements, executes them, and maps results or failures onto an HTTP status/body pair delivered through a CALLBACK_. Every operation has a synchronous variant (which calls the blocking DatabaseController methods) and a drogon::Task coroutine variant (which awaits the *Coro methods on the Drogon IO loop).

Entities are passed by non-const reference because their getSql*Statement(pqxx::params&) methods fill the parameter bag used by the query; the controller does not take ownership of them. The callback is moved into the operation and is invoked exactly once on every path that returns normally, including validation and database failures. CALLBACK_ is std::function<void(int, const std::string&)>, so the first argument is an HTTP status code and the second a response body (usually serialized JSON).

This class is copyable/movable by design: copies share the same DatabaseController through a std::shared_ptr. No mutable per-instance state is touched after construction, so concurrent use of distinct instances is independent; the thread-safety of the shared DatabaseController itself is not specified here.
EntityController, DatabaseController
